newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Corp offered Israel Chem shares.
newsitem.headline: Israel Corp offered Israel Chem shares.

text.p: The Israeli government is offering to sell Israel Corp shares in Israel Chemicals equal to about 17 percent of equity, Israel Corp told the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (TASE) on Monday.

"The company is considering the...offering on the basis of the rights contained in the agreement," Israel Corp said in a statement, referring to the February 1995 accord in which Israel Corp acquired a controlling 24.9 percent of Israel Chemicals from the government.
The Israeli government holds 48.5 percent of Israel Chemicals and the remainder is traded on the TASE.

The sale is one of the main planks of the government's 1997 privatisation programme. The programme also calls for a public offering in Bezeq Israel Telecom and selling Zim Navigation, which the government also controls together with Israel Corp.

Tsipi Livni, the head of the Government Corporations Authority, said Israel Corp had 30 days to respond to the offer. She said that under the terms of the 1995 agreement Israel Corp has the right of first refusal to buy the shares at their average TASE price over the 90 days prior to the sale.

Livni said that if Israel Corp, which is controlled by entrepreneur Shoul Eisenberg, turned down the offer the government would sell their shares by tender or through a series of small public offerings.
At Israel Chemicals current market valuation, the 17 percent holding is worth $222 million. Israel Corp could choose not to buy the full 17 percent under the terms of the agreement.
Israel Corp and Eisenberg acquired in equal parts the original 24.9 percent for $231 million. In December 1996, Eisenberg sold his personal holding to Israel Corp for $128.4 million.
The parliamentary finance committee approved in principle in early February selling up to 20 percent of Israel Chemicals, a chemical-manufacturing holding company.
